clinicalPearls: Immune-mediated destruction of gastric corpus and fundus parietal cells causes achlorhydria and loss of intrinsic factor, sparing the antrum — the defining topographical pattern distinguishing it from Helicobacter-associated multifocal atrophic gastritis.

Presents insidiously with fatigue and iron-deficiency anaemia years before overt vitamin B12 deficiency; iron malabsorption from achlorhydria typically precedes the macrocytic pernicious anaemia phase.
Anti-parietal cell antibodies are sensitive but not specific; anti-intrinsic factor antibodies are highly specific for pernicious anaemia though less sensitive.

Loss of acid-mediated negative feedback drives antral G-cell hyperplasia and hypergastrinaemia, which stimulates enterochromaffin-like (ECL) cell hyperplasia and predisposes to type 1 gastric neuroendocrine tumours.
Strongly clusters with other organ-specific autoimmune disease — autoimmune thyroiditis, type 1 diabetes and vitiligo — so screen a diagnosed patient across endocrine axes.

Endoscopy shows a pale, atrophic corpus with loss of rugal folds and visible submucosal vessels while the antrum looks relatively normal; corpus-predominant biopsies are essential as random sampling may miss the pattern.
Neurological sequelae of B12 deficiency (subacute combined degeneration, peripheral neuropathy, cognitive change) can occur without anaemia and may be irreversible if treatment is delayed.
Confers a modestly increased long-term risk of gastric adenocarcinoma in addition to neuroendocrine tumours, justifying endoscopic surveillance in advanced atrophy.
reference.pathophysiology: Autoimmune gastritis is a T-cell-mediated, organ-specific autoimmune disease directed against the gastric H+/K+-ATPase (proton pump) of oxyntic parietal cells in the corpus and fundus. CD4+ T-helper cells targeting the ATPase subunits drive progressive lymphocytic infiltration, parietal and chief cell apoptosis, and glandular atrophy with replacement by pyloric (pseudopyloric) and intestinal metaplasia. Loss of parietal cells produces two cardinal deficits: achlorhydria, which impairs the ferric-to-ferrous iron conversion and non-haem iron absorption leading to early iron deficiency, and loss of intrinsic factor secretion, which abolishes ileal vitamin B12 uptake and eventually causes pernicious anaemia. Achlorhydria removes the normal acid inhibition of antral gastrin release, so G cells hypersecrete gastrin; sustained hypergastrinaemia is trophic to corpus enterochromaffin-like cells, producing linear and nodular ECL hyperplasia that can progress to type 1 gastric neuroendocrine tumours. The antrum, lacking oxyntic glands, is characteristically spared. There is frequent overlap with Helicobacter pylori-triggered molecular mimicry as an initiating event in some patients, and a strong association with the wider spectrum of autoimmune polyendocrinopathy.
additionalDifferentials: Helicobacter pylori-associated multifocal atrophic gastritis (antral and corpus involvement)
Coeliac disease as an alternative cause of iron and micronutrient malabsorption
Ménétrier disease and other hypertrophic gastropathies
Zollinger-Ellison syndrome as an alternative cause of hypergastrinaemia (with high acid output, not achlorhydria)
Proton pump inhibitor-induced hypergastrinaemia and ECL hyperplasia
Other causes of macrocytic anaemia such as folate deficiency or myelodysplasia
additionalInvestigations: Anti-parietal cell and anti-intrinsic factor antibody testing
Serum vitamin B12 with methylmalonic acid and homocysteine when B12 is borderline
Full blood count and iron studies documenting the iron-deficient then macrocytic sequence
Fasting serum gastrin and chromogranin A as markers of ECL-cell drive
Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy with mapped corpus and antral biopsies (updated Sydney protocol)
Histology with immunostaining for enterochromaffin-like cell hyperplasia and metaplasia grading
Screening of thyroid function and autoantibodies given autoimmune clustering
redFlags: Neurological features of B12 deficiency (paraesthesiae, ataxia, cognitive decline) indicating possible subacute combined degeneration
Endoscopic nodules or polyps suggesting gastric neuroendocrine tumour
New dyspepsia, weight loss or bleeding raising concern for coexisting gastric adenocarcinoma
Severe symptomatic anaemia with cardiorespiratory compromise
Rapidly progressive pancytopenia suggesting profound megaloblastic marrow failure
reference.prognosis: With lifelong vitamin B12 replacement and correction of iron deficiency the haematological outlook is excellent and most symptoms resolve, though established neurological damage may be only partially reversible. The atrophic mucosa persists, so the lifelong risk of gastric neuroendocrine tumours and adenocarcinoma warrants periodic endoscopic surveillance.
pitfalls: Attributing early iron-deficiency anaemia to occult blood loss and overlooking achlorhydria-related malabsorption, delaying diagnosis
Relying on a normal serum B12 to exclude deficiency when functional deficiency (raised methylmalonic acid) is present
Sampling only the antrum at endoscopy and missing corpus-predominant atrophy
Misinterpreting reactive hypergastrinaemia as Zollinger-Ellison syndrome without checking acid status
Failing to screen for and monitor associated autoimmune endocrine disease
references: Standard gastroenterology textbook chapters on chronic atrophic gastritis
International guidance on management of epithelial precancerous conditions of the stomach
Clinical immunology reference texts on organ-specific autoimmunity
management: Lifelong parenteral vitamin B12 (hydroxocobalamin) replacement to correct and prevent pernicious anaemia and neurological injury
Iron replacement for the early iron-deficiency anaemia arising from achlorhydria
Endoscopic surveillance of the atrophic corpus for type 1 gastric neuroendocrine tumours and gastric adenocarcinoma
Management of type 1 gastric neuroendocrine tumours by endoscopic resection and surveillance, with somatostatin analogues in selected cases
Screen for and manage clustered organ-specific autoimmunity such as autoimmune thyroid disease, type 1 diabetes and vitiligo
Monitoring of the haematological response and resolution of symptoms
